# Notes for AI assistants

This folder is the Breezell plugin `{{id}}` ({{displayName}}): a VS Code extension whose `package.json`
has a `breezell` object and which uses `vscode.breezell`.

Before changing anything, read `.agents/skills/breezell-plugin/SKILL.md`, then the reference page in
`.agents/skills/breezell-plugin/references/` for what you touch. The typings of `vscode.breezell` are in
`types/breezell.d.ts`.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm install` | Install the tools |
| `npm run build` / `npm run watch` | Build `src/` into `dist/` (not in a Pack: it has no code) |
| `npm run typecheck` | Type check (not in a Pack) |
| `npm run validate` | Check `package.json` as Breezell reads it |
| `npm run package:open` / `package:closed` | Pack a `.vsix` |

Done means `validate` passes and, for a plugin with code, `typecheck` passes and the build works. Declare only the permissions the code uses,

# {{displayName}}

{{description}}

A [Breezell](https://breezell.com) plugin (`{{id}}`).

## Develop

```bash
npm install
```

Open this folder in Breezell and press **F5**: the plugin runs in a development window.
Plugins run only while you are signed in to Breezell.

- `src/extension.ts` — the plugin. Besides the VS Code API it can use `vscode.breezell`
  (typings in `types/breezell.d.ts`); ask only for the permissions you need in
  `package.json` › `breezell.permissions`.
- `npm run validate` — check `package.json`.

## Package

```bash
npm run package:open     # open source: the source ships in the package
npm run package:closed   # closed source: minified build only, no source
```

Either command writes `{{id}}-<version>.vsix`. Install it in Breezell from
**Plugins › Installed › Install local .vsix**. It works without uploading it anywhere.

## Publish to the Breezell plugin market

1. Fork [BreezellCode/BreezellCode](https://github.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode) and clone your fork.
2. `node tools/breezell-plugin.mjs submit --market <path to your clone>`
3. Commit, push and open a pull request. The market check runs on it.

Guide: <https://github.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode/tree/main/plugins>

description: "Builds and changes Breezell plugins: VS Code extensions with a `breezell` object in package.json that use `vscode.breezell` (the user's conversations, chat models, agent tools and tool call hooks, Breezell's screens, windows) and are packed and published with the Breezell devkit. # Breezell plugins

A Breezell plugin is a VS Code extension whose `package.json` has a `breezell` object. It can use the
whole VS Code API, and `vscode.breezell` for what is Breezell's, limited to the permissions it declares.
Work in this order: understand the request, choose permissions, declare, write code, check, test, pack.
Read the reference page for the part you touch before writing it: they are short and exact.

## 1. Look before you change anything

- `package.json`: the `breezell` object (`apiVersion`, `permissions`, `optionalPermissions`, `source`) and
  `contributes.breezell`.
- `types/breezell.d.ts`: the API this project can call. When a call you need is missing, the copy is old:
  replace it, and `tools/breezell-plugin.mjs` with it, from
  `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode/main/plugins/devkit/breezell.d.ts` and
  `.../devkit/breezell-plugin.mjs`. The pages in `references/` are copies of the market's `plugins/docs`:
  the newest are at `https://github.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode/tree/main/plugins/docs`.
- `src/extension.ts` (none in a Pack) and the scripts in `package.json`.

## 2. From what the user wants to what to use

| The user wants | Permission | Use | Read |
|---|---|---|---|
| Use their chat model (or another of the picker's) | `models.request` | `models.request` | `references/models.md` |
| Know when the AI starts or finishes, no content | `chat.events` (normal) | `chat.onDidStartTurn`, `onDidFinishTurn` | `references/chat.md` |
| Read conversations, tool calls, recalled memories | `chat.read` | `listConversations`, `getConversation`, `onDidChangeConversation`, `listSubagents` | `references/chat.md` |
| Send messages, start conversations, stop a reply, keep work going | `chat.send` | `chat.send`, `chat.stop`, `holdDoneNotice` | `references/chat.md` |
| Start a subagent of a conversation, message it, close it (Breezell newer than 1.4.56) | `chat.send` | `startSubagent`, `messageSubagent`, `closeSubagent` | `references/chat.md` |
| Approve or reject a waiting tool call | `chat.approve` | `chat.approve`, `chat.reject` | `references/chat.md` |
| Change, stop or add context to what the user sends | `chat.intercept` | `chat.registerSendHandler` | `references/chat.md` |
| Read the chat box | `chat.input` | `chat.readInput` | `references/chat.md` |
| Give the agent a tool | `agent.tools` | `contributes.breezell.tools` + `tools.register` | `references/agent.md` |
| See or refuse the agent's tool calls | `agent.hooks` | `tools.registerCallHandler`, `tools.onDidRunTool` | `references/agent.md` |
| Skills, rules, MCP servers with no code | none (`agent.tools` for MCP) | `contributes.breezell.skills`, `rules`, `mcpServers` | `references/agent.md` |
| Buttons, slash menu rows, pages, modes, settings cards | `ui.contribute` (normal) | `contributes.breezell.ui` | `references/ui.md` |
| A tile on Box › Models › Sign in for a service the plugin connects to (Breezell newer than 1.4.64) | `ui.contribute` (normal) | `ui.signIns` + `ui.setSignInStatus` | `references/ui.md` |
| A space of the plugin's own in Box, with pages Breezell draws or its own HTML (Breezell newer than 1.4.691) | `ui.contribute` (normal) | `ui.spaces` + `ui.setState` | `references/ui.md` |
| Answer conversations with an agent the plugin runs (Breezell newer than 1.4.64) | `chat.agent` | `agents.register`, `setModels`, `importConversation` | `references/own-agent.md` |
| Hide, move, restyle or replace Breezell's parts; colours, fonts, a stylesheet; a companion | `ui.modify` | `contributes.breezell.ui` | `references/ui.md` |
| Draw a code fence language | `chat.render` | `ui.renderers` | `references/ui.md` |
| A window of its own, also without the editor | none | `contributes.breezell.windows` + `windows.open` | `references/windows.md` |
| The model picker | `models.select` (normal) | `models.list`, `models.select` | `references/models.md` |
| Custom APIs without keys / with keys | `providers.list` (normal) / `providers.read` | `providers.list` / `providers.listCustom` | `references/models.md` |
| A restart | `app.restart` (normal), `app.forceRestart` | `app.requestRestart`, `contributes.breezell.restart` | `references/restart.md` |
| A theme or a file preview for the Breezell phone app (not an extension: one `phone-plugin.json`, no code) | none | `init --template phone`, `phone-validate`, `phone-submit` | `references/phone.md` |

Every permission: `references/permissions.md`. Every call: `references/api.md`. Errors: `references/errors.md`.
Limits: `references/limits.md`. Whole examples to start from: `references/recipes.md`.

## 3. Rules that hold everywhere

- **Fewest permissions.** Declare only what the code uses. A permission newer than the user's Breezell
  refuses the install from `permissions`: put new ones (`agent.hooks`, `providers.list`, ...) in
  `optionalPermissions` and check `vscode.breezell.permissions` before using them.
- **Expect refusals.** Dangerous permissions are asked at first use and can be turned off any time. Catch
  errors, check `error.name` (`BreezellPermissionDenied`, `BreezellNotSignedIn`, ...), and tell the user what
  the plugin cannot do. Never retry in a loop.
- **Check for the API.** `vscode.breezell` is undefined outside Breezell; plugins run only while signed in.
- **Declare, do not inject.** Breezell's own window runs no plugin script or CSS. Change its screens only
  through `contributes.breezell.ui` (or a stylesheet, which is read as declarations); a plugin's own UI goes
  in a page (`ui.surfaces`), a webview or a window.
- **Never touch** Breezell's internal commands (`breezell.*`), its sign-in, plan, quota, custom API,
  approvals or errors, or its files (sign-ins, conversations, memories). Never imitate its sign-in or
  payment screens or work around billing. These are refused, and review rejects plugins that try.
- **Private data stays put.** What `chat.read`, `chat.input`, `chat.intercept`, `agent.hooks` and agent tools
  hand over stays on the user's computer unless the README says where it goes. Keys from `providers.listCustom`
  go only to their provider. Secrets go in `context.secrets`.
- **Be quick where Breezell waits.** A send handler or tool call handler that takes over 3 seconds is passed
  over. Do slow work before or after, not in them.
- **Start with Breezell** (`"activationEvents": ["onStartupFinished"]`) when registering tools, a send handler
  or a tool call handler: nothing is offered before the code is registered.
- **Remote windows:** `"extensionKind": ["ui", "workspace"]`.
- **Market text is English:** README, package.json texts, commit messages. Translations go in `i18n/`
  (`references/translations.md`).

## 4. Before saying it is done

1. `npm run validate`: no problems. Everything it reports, Breezell would leave out.
2. `npm run typecheck`: no errors (a Pack has no code and no such script).
3. `npm run build`: it builds (not in a Pack).
4. Each permission is used and explained in the README; each call's errors are handled.
5. Tell the user how to try it: open the folder in Breezell, press **F5**, sign in in the development window,
   and what to do there. Say which permissions Breezell will ask for.
6. To install it for real: `npm run package:open` (or `package:closed`), then **Plugins › Installed › Install
   local .vsix**. To publish: `references/publishing.md`.

## 5. Mistakes seen often

- A turn event's `conversationId` is not the id of `listConversations`: use `chat.conversationOfTurn(turnId)`.
- An `automated` message after the user pressed Stop fails with `BreezellStoppedByUser` until they write again.
- `chat.send` refuses a conversation that is busy; wait for `onDidFinishTurn`.
- `models.request` runs at most 2 at a time and 20 a minute per plugin.
- Tool parameters and results from `chat.read` are cut at 20,000 characters (`resultLength` is the real length).
- A must-read colour pair (`send-bg`/`send-fg`, `approve-*`, `reject-*`, `error-*`, `accent`/`accent-fg`) is used
  only when both are written out, opaque and contrast at least 4.5.
- A setting a look follows (`when`, `variants`, a token `{ "setting" }`) must be the plugin's own, in
  `contributes.configuration`.
- Values crossing to Breezell are JSON: no functions, class instances or `Date` objects.

## References

All in `references/`, the same pages as the market's `plugins/docs`:

`README.md` (index), `getting-started.md`, `manifest.md`, `permissions.md`, `api.md`, `errors.md`, `limits.md`,
`chat.md`, `models.md`, `agent.md`, `own-agent.md`, `ui.md`, `windows.md`, `restart.md`, `translations.md`, `security.md`,
`publishing.md`, `recipes.md`.

# Breezell plugin documentation

Everything you need to build a Breezell plugin, from the first command to the market. The
[market overview](https://github.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode/blob/main/plugins/README.md) is the short version; these pages are the whole of it. They are also
the reference of the AI skill every new plugin ships with (see [Working with an AI assistant](#working-with-an-ai-assistant)).

Typings: [`devkit/breezell.d.ts`](https://github.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode/blob/main/plugins/devkit/breezell.d.ts)
(in a plugin made from a template: `types/breezell.d.ts`).

## Read in this order

| Page | What it covers |
|---|---|
| [Getting started](getting-started.md) | Make a plugin, run it, check it, pack it, install it |
| [package.json](manifest.md) | The `breezell` object, `contributes.breezell`, how a plugin opens |
| [Permissions](permissions.md) | Every permission, which are asked for, what each gives |
| [API reference](api.md) | Every call of `vscode.breezell`, with its permission and limits |
| [Errors](errors.md) | What each error name means and what to do |
| [Limits](limits.md) | Every limit in one table |

## By topic

| Page | What it covers |
|---|---|
| [The chat](chat.md) | Turn events, reading conversations, sending, stopping, work over many turns, a message before it is sent |
| [Models and providers](models.md) | The user's models: requests, streaming, images, JSON; the model picker; custom APIs |
| [The agent](agent.md) | Packs (skills, rules, MCP servers), agent tools, watching and refusing the agent's tool calls |
| [An agent of your own](own-agent.md) | Answering conversations with an agent the plugin runs: its models in the picker, turns, tool calls, approvals, Breezell's tools for it, sessions |
| [Breezell's screens](ui.md) | Buttons, the slash menu, pages, a companion, settings, patches, tokens, fonts, a stylesheet, variants, code fences, modes, sign-in tiles |
| [Windows](windows.md) | Windows of the plugin's own, also without an editor |
| [Phone plugins](phone.md) | Themes and file previews for the Breezell phone app, written as data: the manifest, palettes, viewers, publishing |
| [Restarting Breezell](restart.md) | Asking for a restart, after an install or an update too |
| [Translations](translations.md) | The README, name, description and commands in other languages |
| [Security](security.md) | What plugins cannot reach, and what users and review expect |
| [Publishing](publishing.md) | Open or closed source, the market, review, the blocklist |
| [Recipes](recipes.md) | Whole small plugins for common tasks |

## Versions

A plugin declares the API generation it was written for in `breezell.apiVersion` (1). Breezell adds to
generation 1 without breaking it; pages mark what needs a newer Breezell. A permission an older Breezell
does not know refuses the install when it is in `permissions`, so put new ones in `optionalPermissions`
and check `vscode.breezell.permissions` (or a call's error) before using them. Fields an older Breezell
does not know in `contributes.breezell` are ignored, so declaring them is safe.

## Working with an AI assistant

Every plugin made from a template (in Breezell or with `breezell-plugin.mjs init`) has:

- `.agents/skills/breezell-plugin/`: a skill with the workflow, the rules and these pages as its
  references. Breezell's own agent finds it in the plugin's folder, as do tools that read `.agents/skills`.
- `AGENTS.md`, and `CLAUDE.md` pointing to it: what any assistant should read first.

Ask the assistant for what you want ("a panel that lists the files the agent changed"); the skill tells it
which permissions that needs, which calls to use, and to run `npm run validate` and `npm run typecheck`
before it says it is done. The same pages are here for you to read.

# The agent

What a plugin gives Breezell's agent, and how it watches what the agent does.

## Packs: skills, rules, MCP servers

Declare them in `package.json`; no code is needed:

```json
"contributes": {
	"breezell": {
		"skills": ["skills"],
		"rules": ["rules/house-rules.md"],
		"mcpServers": {
			"sequential-thinking": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking"] },
			"docs": { "url": "https://example.com/mcp" }
		}
	},
	"themes": [{ "label": "My Theme", "uiTheme": "vs-dark", "path": "./themes/my-theme.json" }]
}
```

- `skills`: folders holding skill folders (`skills/<name>/SKILL.md`). They appear in Breezell's skill list
  labelled with the plugin, and the agent loads them like any skill. A user's skill of the same name wins.
- `rules`: Markdown files added to the AI's instructions while the plugin is on (at most 8,000 characters
  per file and 24,000 for all plugins together). Keep them short: they count against every request.
  A rule can also wait for one of the plugin's own settings and be meant for some models only *(new)*:

  ```json
  "rules": [
  	{ "path": "rules/tone.md", "when": { "setting": "myTone.mode", "value": "gpt" }, "models": ["*gpt*"] },
  	{ "path": "rules/tone.md", "when": { "setting": "myTone.mode", "value": "all" } }
  ]
  ```

  `when` names a setting in your own `contributes.configuration` and a value of its type; put the setting in
  Feature Options (`ui.options`) so users can switch it. `models` lists model names, with `*` for any run of
  characters and case ignored, matched against the whole name of the model the request goes to (up to 16).
  The rule goes in while both hold, from the next request on; a file named by several rules goes in once.
  Breezell versions from before conditional rules leave such entries out.
- `mcpServers`: a `command` (with `args` and `env`) or a `url` (with `headers`). They appear in the MCP list
  labelled with the plugin; a user or project server of the same name wins. Users see each command before
  they install. MCP servers give the agent tools, so they need the `agent.tools` permission in
  `breezell.permissions`: they start once the user allows it.

Everything a plugin declares goes away when it is turned off or removed, and while nobody is signed in.

## Agent tools

A plugin can give Breezell's agent tools of its own: it declares each one in `package.json`, with
the chat modes it is offered in, and runs it in its code. It needs the `agent.tools` permission
("Agent tool registration"), which the user is asked for when the plugin first registers a tool.

```json
"activationEvents": ["onStartupFinished"],
"breezell": { "apiVersion": 1, "permissions": ["agent.tools"] },
"contributes": {
	"breezell": {
		"tools": [{
			"name": "get_weather",
			"displayName": "Weather",
			"description": "Current weather for a city. Use it when the user asks about the weather.",
			"modes": ["chat", "agent", "entanglement"],
			"inputSchema": {
				"type": "object",
				"properties": { "city": { "type": "string", "description": "City name" } },
				"required": ["city"]
			}
		}]
	}
}
```

```ts
context.subscriptions.push(vscode.breezell.tools.register('get_weather', {
	async invoke(input, token) {
		const weather = await lookUp(String(input.city), token);
		return weather ? `${weather.summary}, ${weather.celsius} °C` : { text: 'No such city', isError: true };
	},
}));
```

- `name`: 2 to 48 lowercase letters, digits and underscores, not one of Breezell's own tool names. At
  most 16 tools. `description` is what the agent reads to decide when to call it; `inputSchema` is an
  object JSON Schema (left out: no arguments); `displayName` is what the user sees.
- `modes`: one or several of `chat`, `agent`, `entanglement`, `analyze`, `teams` (none: `agent`). In
  any other mode the agent neither sees nor can call the tool, so a set of tools can make a mode of
  its own, for example Chat with a few tools of yours.
- Register the code when the plugin starts (`onStartupFinished`): a tool is offered only while its code
  is registered. Disposing the registration takes it away.
- The agent reaches the tools as those of the MCP server `plugin:<publisher.name>`; the user's "MCP
  tools" auto-approve setting applies to their calls. `input` is checked against `inputSchema`
  first (required properties present; undeclared ones removed unless the schema allows
  `additionalProperties`).
- `invoke` returns text, or `{ text, isError: true }` for a failure the agent should see as one; a
  thrown error is a failure too. Results longer than 400,000 characters are cut. `token` is
  cancelled when the user stops the agent or after 5 minutes.
- If the user refuses, the tools stay registered but unused; turning the permission on later under
  **Plugins › Installed** brings them back at once. Signed out, blocklisted or turned off, nothing is
  offered, and each call is checked again.
- With `chat.read`, a conversation shows each call of a plugin's tool with `plugin: { id, name }`.
- The arguments the agent passes can hold conversation text or file contents: keep them on the user's
  computer unless the tool says otherwise. Review looks closely at plugins with agent tools.

[Chat Mirror](https://github.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode/tree/main/plugins/examples/chat-mirror) has two: `pin_note` (Chat, Agent, Entanglement) and `list_notes`
(every mode).

### The agent's tool calls

With `agent.hooks` a plugin sees each tool call of the agent after Breezell's own checks and before it
runs or asks for approval, and can refuse it:

```js
vscode.breezell.tools.registerCallHandler(call => {
	if (call.name === 'run_terminal_cmd' && /rm -rf/.test(String(call.params.command))) {
		return { deny: true, reason: 'No deleting in this repository.' };
	}
	// or nothing: the call goes on
});
vscode.breezell.tools.onDidRunTool(run => console.log(run.name, run.status, run.resultLength));
```

- A call is `{ conversationId, toolCallId, name, params, mcpServer, mode }`; each text in `params` is cut at
  20,000 characters. `conversationId` is the one `listConversations` uses.
- A refused call never runs. The agent reads your plugin's reason, is told not to repeat the call, and the user
  sees it as your plugin's. Repeating the same refused call counts toward Breezell's loop guard.
- An answer later than 3 seconds, or a failure, lets the call go on; all plugins together get at most 6 seconds,
  in id order, and the first refusal decides. A Stop pressed meanwhile ends the call.
- `onDidRunTool` reports each call once its row has finished: `done`, `failed` or `rejected` (by the user), with
  what the chat shows of the result (cut at 20,000 characters, `resultLength` the full length).

# API reference

Every member of `vscode.breezell`, with the permission it needs. The typings are
[`breezell.d.ts`](https://github.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode/blob/main/plugins/devkit/breezell.d.ts)
(in a plugin made from a template: `types/breezell.d.ts`); this page says what the typings cannot.

`vscode.breezell` is `undefined` in other editors and in Breezell versions without the plugin API, so
check it first. A call fails with an `Error` whose `name` says why ([Errors](errors.md)): check the name,
not the message, which may change.

```ts
const breezell = vscode.breezell;
if (!breezell) {
	return; // not Breezell
}
try {
	await breezell.chat.send('Hello');
} catch (error) {
	if ((error as Error).name === 'BreezellPermissionDenied') { /* say what the plugin cannot do */ }
}
```

## Top level

| Member | Permission | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `apiVersion` | none | The API generation this Breezell implements (`1`) |
| `permissions` | none | The permissions this plugin declared (with the optional ones this Breezell knows) |
| `permissionState(p)` | declared `p` | `granted`, `denied` or `ask`; asks no one |
| `requestPermission(p)` | declared `p` | Asks the user when it is the first time; whether it is allowed |
| `onDidChangePermissions` | none | The user changed one of this plugin's permissions (after one of the two calls above) |
| `language`, `onDidChangeLanguage` | none | Breezell's display language: `en`, `zh-CN`, `zh-TW`, `ja`, `ko`, `ru`, `es`, `pt-BR`. `vscode.env.language` does not follow it. Empty for a moment at start |

## `account`

| Member | Permission | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `isSignedIn`, `onDidChangeSignIn` | none | Whether a Breezell account is signed in. Plugins run only while one is |

## `app`

| Member | Permission | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `requestRestart({ scope, reason, l10n, force })` | `app.restart`; `app.forceRestart` with `force` | Ask to restart `extensionHost`, `window` or `app`, or with `force` restart without asking (once per plugin version). `true` when it will happen. See [Restarting Breezell](restart.md) |
| `focus()`, `onDidChangeFocus` | none | `{ editorFocused, lastUsed, windowId }`: whether the user is in Breezell, whether this editor window is the one used last, and its id. See [Several editor windows](windows.md#several-editor-windows) |

## `chat`

| Member | Permission | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `onDidStartTurn`, `onDidFinishTurn` | `chat.events` | `{ turnId, conversationId, mode }`; a finish adds `outcome` (`completed`, `error`, `stopped`) and `durationMs`. No content |
| `conversationOfTurn(turnId)` | `chat.read` | The `listConversations` id of a turn event's conversation; undefined for a turn too long ago (the last 200 are kept) |
| `listConversations()` | `chat.read` | This workspace's conversations, most recently changed first: `id`, `title`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `messageCount`, `current`, `activity`, `backgroundCommands`, `subagent` (set on a subagent's conversation; Breezell newer than 1.4.56) |
| `getConversation(id)` | `chat.read` | The same with `messages`, `streaming` and `usage` |
| `onDidChangeConversation` | `chat.read` | `{ conversationId, activity, streaming, backgroundCommands, subagent }`, at most every 150 ms per conversation |
| `show(id)` | `chat.read` | Opens the conversation in Breezell's chat |
| `readInput()` | `chat.input` | The chat box: `text`, `before` (before the caret), `recent` (last messages' text) |
| `registerSendHandler(handler)` | `chat.intercept` | See each message the user sends before it goes: change it, stop it, add context for the AI. One per plugin. See [A message before it is sent](chat.md#a-message-before-it-is-sent) |
| `send(text, options)` | `chat.send` | Send as the user would: `conversationId` (none: a new one), `automated`, `mode`, `model`, `attachments`. Resolves to `{ conversationId }` once the message is in |
| `stop(id)` | `chat.send` | Stops the reply being written; not the user's Stop |
| `listSubagents(conversationId)` | `chat.read` | A conversation's subagents, open and closed, oldest first: `id`, `leadConversationId`, `name`, `mode`, `status`, `createdAt`, `startedBy`, `closedBy`. Breezell newer than 1.4.56. See [Subagents](chat.md#subagents-chatread-chatsend) |
| `startSubagent(conversationId, { name, task, model })` | `chat.send` | Start a subagent of a conversation in Agent or Entanglement mode: a conversation of its own that works on `task` and reports to its lead. Resolves to `{ conversationId }`. Breezell newer than 1.4.56 |

### Conversation messages

`getConversation(id).messages` is what the chat shows, in order; `index` is the row's position.

| `kind` | Fields |
|---|---|
| `user` | `text`, `time`, `attachments` (names), `recalledMemories` (`id`, `summary`, `detail`, `priority`, `source`), `memoryUse` (`resident`, `relevant`, `complete`, `inThisConversation`), `automatedBy` (a plugin's message: `{ id, name }`) |
| `assistant` | `text`, `reasoning`, `usage` (`inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`) |
| `tool` | `id`, `name`, `status` (`invalid`, `awaitingApproval`, `running`, `done`, `failed`, `rejected`), `params`, `result` (cut at 20,000 characters), `resultLength`, `mcpServer`, `plugin` (`{ id, name }` for a plugin's tool) |
| `error` | `text` |

`usage` on a conversation adds `replies` and `repliesWithoutUsage`. Token counts are the provider's, for a
budget of your own: some providers count cache reads inside `inputTokens`. A conversation's `usage` also holds what its helpers
spent, subagents included (Breezell newer than 1.4.56); checks that run beside a conversation are not in it.

## What every call shares

- Each call checks, at that moment: a signed-in account, the plugin not on the blocklist, the permission
  declared and allowed. A plugin that was running when one of these changed keeps running but gets nothing.
- Events reach a plugin only while it may receive them: turning a permission off stops them at once.
- Values cross between processes as JSON: functions and class instances do not, `Date`s become strings.

# The chat

What a plugin can know and do about the user's conversations. Each call names its permission; see
[API reference](api.md#chat) for the exact shapes.

## Turn events (`chat.events`)

```ts
vscode.breezell.chat.onDidStartTurn(turn => status.text = `Working (${turn.mode})`);
vscode.breezell.chat.onDidFinishTurn(turn => status.text = `${turn.outcome} in ${Math.round(turn.durationMs / 1000)} s`);
```

- A turn starts when the AI starts answering and finishes as `completed`, `error` or `stopped`. A turn
  waiting for the user's approval has not finished.
- `conversationId` in an event is stable per conversation in this window but is **not** the id
  `listConversations` uses; with `chat.read`, `conversationOfTurn(turnId)` gives that id.
- Events carry no content: the mode, the outcome and the duration. `chat.events` is normal: on unless the
  user turns it off.

## Reading conversations (`chat.read`)

```ts
const list = await vscode.breezell.chat.listConversations();           // most recently changed first
const open = list.find(c => c.current);
const conversation = open && await vscode.breezell.chat.getConversation(open.id);
for (const message of conversation?.messages ?? []) {
	if (message.kind === 'tool') { console.log(message.name, message.status, message.resultLength); }
}
vscode.breezell.chat.onDidChangeConversation(change => console.log(change.conversationId, change.activity));
```

- What the user sees in the chat of this workspace: their messages (with the memories recalled for
  each), replies with reasoning, each tool call with its parameters, status and result, and errors.
  Never Breezell's prompts, text only the model sees, hidden rows or other workspaces' conversations.
- A tool's parameters and result are cut at 20,000 characters (`resultLength` is the full length).
- `activity` is `idle`, `thinking`, `writing`, `runningTool`, `awaitingApproval` or `working`. A
  conversation waiting for its own analysis subagents or teammates is `working` (Breezell newer than
  1.4.54; earlier versions say `awaitingApproval`, though nothing waits for the user).
  `onDidChangeConversation` fires at most every 150 ms per conversation while it streams, with the
  reply being written in `streaming`.
- A subagent's conversation (see [Subagents](#subagents-chatread-chatsend)) is listed like any other, with `subagent` set on
  it and on its changes.
- `show(id)` opens a conversation in Breezell's chat. `readInput()` (`chat.input`) gives what is typed in
  the chat box, its part before the caret, and the text of the last messages.

## Sending (`chat.send`)

```ts
const { conversationId } = await vscode.breezell.chat.send('Run the tests and fix what fails', {
	mode: 'agent',                                                 // normal, agent or plan
	model: { provider: 'openAICompatible', model: 'my-model' },     // one of models.list()
	attachments: ['src/app.ts', 'docs/screen.png'],                 // files of the workspace
});
await vscode.breezell.chat.stop(conversationId);                // stops the reply being written
```

- Without `conversationId` a new conversation starts. The call resolves once the message is in the
  conversation; the reply follows through `onDidChangeConversation`.
- The AI answers it as if the user had typed it, with the same tools, and it is billed the same way.
  At most 10 messages a minute per plugin; a busy conversation refuses it (`BreezellInvalidRequest`).
- `mode` and `model` are set as the user's pickers set them: in the conversation open in the chat the
  picker moves; another conversation keeps them as its own. Entanglement, Agent Teams and Dark Selene
  stay the user's choice. `model` must be one of `models.list()`.
- `attachments`: up to 10 files or folders of the workspace, by absolute path or relative to its first
  folder; images (png, jpg, gif, webp, up to 10 MB) go as images. Links, anything outside the workspace
  folders and what Breezell keeps from plugins are refused.
- `stop(id)` is not the user's Stop: `automated` messages may follow it.
- `approve(id)` / `reject(id)` (`chat.approve`) answer the tool call a conversation waits for. Leave
  approving to the user unless approving is what the plugin is for.

## Subagents (`chat.read`, `chat.send`)

A subagent is a conversation of its own that a conversation in Agent or Entanglement mode (its **lead**)
starts. It works on one task in the lead's mode, fixed when it starts, and reports back to the lead. Users
see it in its own tab beside the lead's; a plugin sees it as a conversation with `subagent` set. All of
this needs a Breezell newer than 1.4.56: check that `startSubagent` exists before calling it.

```ts
const { chat } = vscode.breezell;
if (typeof chat.startSubagent !== 'function') { return; }          // an older Breezell

const { conversationId: subagentId } = await chat.startSubagent(leadId, {
	name: 'Check the docs',
	task: 'Read docs/*.md and list every link that no longer works. Report the list.',
	model: { provider: 'openAICompatible', model: 'my-model' },     // one of models.list(); needed when the user picks each subagent's model
});

chat.onDidChangeConversation(change => {
	if (change.conversationId === subagentId && change.subagent) {
		console.log(change.subagent.status);                            // working, awaitingApproval, idle, interrupted or closed
	}
});

await chat.messageSubagent(subagentId, 'Skip the old/ folder');        // { delivered: 'nextStep' } while it works, 'started' when idle
const open = (await chat.listSubagents(leadId)).filter(s => s.status !== 'closed');
await chat.closeSubagent(subagentId);                               // true; false when it was closed already
```

- `listSubagents(conversationId)` (`chat.read`) gives a conversation's subagents, open and closed, oldest
  first. Each has `id` (its conversation, as `listConversations` names it), `leadConversationId`, `name`,
  `mode` (`agent` or `entanglement`), `status` (`working`, `awaitingApproval`, `idle`, `interrupted` or
  `closed`), `createdAt`, `startedBy` (the plugin that started it; absent when the lead's AI did) and
  `closedBy` (`agent`, `user`, `withdrawn` or `plugin`, once closed).
- `startSubagent(conversationId, { name?, task, model? })` (`chat.send`) starts one and resolves to
  `{ conversationId }`, the subagent's own. `task` is everything it is told: it sees nothing of the
  conversation, so write it self-contained. `name` is at most 60 characters and is made unique among the
  conversation's open subagents. It reports to the lead's AI as the subagents the AI starts itself do, and the
  AI is told that a plugin started it.
- `messageSubagent(subagentId, text)` (`chat.send`) sends a message to an open subagent. It shows in the
  subagent's conversation as the plugin's, never as the user's or the lead's, and resolves to
  `{ delivered }`: `'nextStep'` when the subagent was working and reads it at its next step, `'started'` when
  it was idle and starts on it.
- `closeSubagent(subagentId)` (`chat.send`) stops a subagent. Its conversation stays in the history, and the
  lead's AI is told that the plugin closed it. It resolves to `false` when it was closed already.
- `getConversation(subagentId)` and `onDidChangeConversation` (`chat.read`) read a subagent like any
  conversation, with `subagent` set on the summary and on each change. `show(subagentId)` opens it in its tab.
- `send(text, { conversationId: subagentId })` also works while the subagent is open, but it fails once the
  subagent is closed, and with `mode` (a subagent keeps the mode it started in). Prefer `messageSubagent`,
  which also reaches a subagent that is working.
- A conversation's `usage` includes what its subagents spent.

What is refused:

- `startSubagent` fails with `BreezellStoppedByUser` after the user pressed Stop in the lead conversation,
  and `messageSubagent` after they pressed Stop in that subagent, until they write there again.
- At most 5 subagents of a conversation work at once; a sixth `startSubagent` fails with
  `BreezellInvalidRequest` until one finishes or is closed.
- A conversation in Plan, Chat or Agent Teams mode has no subagents: `startSubagent` fails with
  `BreezellInvalidRequest`.
- With the **Subagent Model** switch off in Box (the user picks each subagent's model), a start must name a
  `model` from `models.list()`; with it on, `model` is optional and the subagent uses the conversation's own.
- A closed subagent takes no message: `messageSubagent` fails with `BreezellInvalidRequest`.
- `startSubagent` and `messageSubagent` count against the same 10 messages a minute per plugin as `send`
  (`BreezellRateLimited`).
- Whatever a plugin sends this way is the plugin's: labelled with its name in the chat, never taken as the
  user's own words or reaction.

## Work over many turns

A plugin can keep a conversation going until something is done, as the [Goal](https://github.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode/tree/main/plugins/examples/goal) example
does. All of this needs a Breezell newer than 1.4.41, and every call is checked against the sign-in and
the plugin's permissions: after a sign-out or a block it hears nothing more and can do nothing more.

```js
const { chat } = vscode.breezell;
await chat.holdDoneNotice(id);                               // no "done" sound for each turn
chat.onDidFinishTurn(async turn => {
	if (await chat.conversationOfTurn(turn.turnId) !== id) return;
	if (turn.outcome !== 'completed') { await chat.releaseDoneNotice(id); return; }   // stopped, or it failed
	const { backgroundCommands, usage } = await chat.getConversation(id);
	if (backgroundCommands?.willEnd) return;                   // its end starts a turn by itself
	if (done(usage)) { await chat.releaseDoneNotice(id, { announce: true }); return; }
	await chat.send('Go on with the tests', { conversationId: id, automated: true });
});
```

- **`automated`** is for a message the plugin sends on its own. It shows in the chat labelled with the
  plugin's name, and the AI is told the user did not type it. It does not count as the user reacting to the
  last turn and does not end up in their memories. Leave it out only for what a person asked to send.
- **Stop holds.** After the user presses Stop on the reply, an automated message fails with
  `BreezellStoppedByUser` until they write again. A message of theirs waiting in the queue goes first: yours
  fails with `BreezellInvalidRequest`, and the end of that turn is your next chance.
- **The done notice** can be held back, and comes once when released with `announce`. Errors still sound.
  A hold ends by itself on Stop, a sign-out, losing `chat.send`, a block, or the plugin stopping.
- **`backgroundCommands`** (`{ running, willEnd }`) says how many commands run in the background, and how
  many of them will end by themselves: servers and watchers do not. It is a count, not what they are.
- **`usage`** on a reply, on a conversation and on a `models.request` answer is the provider's numbers.
  Some providers count cache reads inside `inputTokens`. A conversation's `usage` also holds what the
  helpers working for it spent (its subagents, its analysis subagents, a lead's teammates, DarkSelene investigators),
  and it grows while they work, before the lead's turn ends (Breezell newer than 1.4.54; earlier
  versions count its own replies only, and its subagents are counted from Breezell newer than 1.4.56). Checks that run beside a conversation (Cross-Check, your own
  `models.request`) are not in it, and `repliesWithoutUsage` says how many replies reported nothing.
- A turn's `outcome` is `completed`, `error` or `stopped`. A turn waiting for the user's approval, or for
  the conversation's subagents or teammates, has not finished, and a plugin should leave approving to the user.

## A message before it is sent

```js
vscode.breezell.chat.registerSendHandler(({ conversationId, text }) => {
	if (/sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}/.test(text)) {
		return { cancel: true, reason: 'This message seems to hold a secret key.' };
	}
	return { text: text.replace(/\bTODO\b/g, 'to do') };   // or nothing: as it is
});
```

Needs `chat.intercept`, one handler per plugin. It covers what the user sends (typed, queued, edited or a
follow-up they picked), not what Breezell or another plugin writes: a teammate's start, a plan's prompt,
`chat.send`. The message goes on through the usual send path, so its model, plan and billing are what they
would have been.

- It sees the text as it reads, with mentions written out (`@file.ts`), and `attachments`: the names of what goes with it. Attachments stay as they are.
- `slashCommand` *(new)*: `{ name }` when the message was sent with one of your own `ui.slashCommands` rows
  (one without `command`), picked in the chat box or typed at the start and shown there as a tag; the text
  still begins with `/name`. `null` when the text merely reads `/name` (pasted, or left as words): that is not
  your command. Absent on an older Breezell, where the text is all there is to go by.
- Context for the AI: answer `{ context: '...' }` (alone or with `text`), up to 20,000 characters, 50,000 from all
  plugins together. The AI reads it with the message and is told it came from your plugin; the user does not see
  it in the chat and `chat.read` does not show it. It stays in the conversation's history, and an edit of the
  message asks your handler again and replaces it.
- Stopped: the user is told by which plugin and why, and the text stays in the chat box.
- A command of the plugin's own: answer `{ cancel: true, handled: true }`. The box clears and nothing is said,
  so telling the user what happened is up to the plugin. Keep `reason` for an older Breezell, which takes it as stopped.
- Changed: what is sent is what shows in the bubble, and it must not be empty or over 400,000 characters.
- An answer later than 3 seconds, or a failure, passes the message on as it was, and all plugins together get
  at most 6 seconds.
- With several plugins they go in id order, each seeing what the one before made of it.

# Errors

Every failed `vscode.breezell` call throws an `Error` whose `name` is one of these. Check the name.

| `name` | When | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `BreezellNotSignedIn` | Nobody is signed in to Breezell | Wait for `account.onDidChangeSignIn`; do nothing meanwhile |
| `BreezellPermissionDenied` | The permission is not declared, or the user refused it or turned it off | Say what the plugin cannot do; offer `requestPermission` where it makes sense |
| `BreezellBlocked` | The plugin is on the market's blocklist | Nothing: every call fails until the user removes it |
| `BreezellNotAPlugin` | The extension has no `breezell` object in its `package.json` | Add it ([package.json](manifest.md)) |
| `BreezellInvalidRequest` | The call's arguments are wrong: no such conversation, a busy conversation, a model the picker does not offer, a refused attachment, a message too long | Fix the call; its message says what |
| `BreezellRateLimited` | Over a per-plugin limit: requests a minute, requests at a time, messages a minute | Wait and try again later; do not retry in a tight loop |
| `BreezellNoModel` | No chat model is selected and the request named none | Ask the user to pick a model, or pass `model` |
| `BreezellModelError` | The model failed: the provider's error, no answer in time, the API stopped answering, or no JSON when `responseFormat: 'json'` asked for it | Tell the user; retry once if it makes sense |
| `BreezellCancelled` | The request's cancellation token fired, or the extension host is going away | Nothing |
| `BreezellStoppedByUser` | An `automated` message after the user pressed Stop, before they wrote again | Wait for the user's next message |
| `BreezellPlanRequired` | `providers.listCustom()` for an account whose plan does not include Custom API | Say so; the user is not asked |

A plugin's own errors inside a tool (`invoke`), a send handler or a tool call handler never reach the user
as Breezell's: a tool's failure reaches the agent as a failed call, a handler's failure lets the message or
the call go on as it was.

# Getting started

From nothing to a plugin installed in your own Breezell. A plugin is a VS Code extension with a
`breezell` object in its `package.json` ([package.json](manifest.md)); everything VS Code extensions can
do, it can do, and `vscode.breezell` adds what is Breezell's ([API reference](api.md)).

**In Breezell**

Open **Breezell Console › Plugins › Develop**, fill in the id and name, choose a template (Pack,
Panel, AI command, Window or Minimal) and how to publish it (open or closed source), then pick a
folder. Open the new folder in a new window.

**From the command line** (Node.js 18 or later)

```bash
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode/main/plugins/devkit/breezell-plugin.mjs
node breezell-plugin.mjs init my-plugin --id my-name.my-plugin --display-name "My Plugin" --template webview
cd my-plugin
npm install
```

Then open the folder in Breezell and press **F5**: the plugin runs in a development window.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run build` / `npm run watch` | Bundle `src/extension.ts` into `dist/extension.js` with esbuild |
| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript type check |
| `npm run validate` | Check `package.json` |
| `npm run package:open` | Pack as **open source**: the source and source maps ship in the package |
| `npm run package:closed` | Pack as **closed source**: minified code only (including the js and css in `media/`), no source, no source maps |
| `npm run submit -- --market <clone of the market>` | Add the package to the market (see "Publishing") |

## What a new plugin holds

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `package.json` | The manifest: `breezell` (API version, permissions, source) and `contributes` |
| `src/extension.ts` | The plugin's code (`activate`, `deactivate`); not in a Pack |
| `types/breezell.d.ts` | The typings of `vscode.breezell`. Replace it with the market's newest copy when you need newer calls |
| `tools/breezell-plugin.mjs` | The devkit: `validate`, `pack`, `submit`. Replace it with the market's newest copy with the typings |
| `.agents/skills/breezell-plugin/` | The skill for an AI assistant, with these pages as references |
| `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | What an AI assistant reads first |
| `.vscode/launch.json`, `tasks.json` | F5 runs the plugin in a development window |
| `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` | Shown on the plugin's market page; `i18n/` holds translations ([Translations](translations.md)) |

## Run it

1. `npm install`, then open the folder in Breezell.
2. Press **F5**. A development window opens with the plugin running; set breakpoints in `src/`.
3. Sign in to Breezell in that window: plugins run only while someone is signed in, and every
   `vscode.breezell` call fails with `BreezellNotSignedIn` otherwise.
4. Change the code, then **Developer: Restart Extension Host** (or reload the window) to run it again.
   `npm run watch` rebuilds as you save.

The plugin's log lines (`console.log`) are in **Help › Toggle Developer Tools** of the development window,
and Breezell's own lines about plugins start with `[BreezellPlugins]` in the **Window** output channel:
a declaration Breezell left out says why there.

## Check it

- `npm run validate` checks `package.json` the way Breezell reads it: permissions, every
  `contributes.breezell` entry, files it names. What it reports, Breezell would leave out.
- `npm run typecheck` checks the code against the typings.
- A permission the plugin uses must be declared; `validate` names the missing ones.

## Install it

`npm run package:open` (or `package:closed`) writes `<publisher.name>-<version>.vsix`. In Breezell,
**Plugins › Installed › Install local .vsix** installs it. A local plugin works the same as one from
the market; the user is told it was not reviewed.

## Before you publish

- [ ] `validate` and `typecheck` pass; the plugin does what it says with every permission turned off too
      (it says what it cannot do instead of failing silently).
- [ ] Only the permissions it needs, each explained in the README.
- [ ] It works in a remote (WSL, SSH) window: `"extensionKind": ["ui", "workspace"]`.
- [ ] It handles being signed out, blocked, and a call failing with each [error](errors.md) it can meet.
- [ ] The README says what it does, in English, with translations if you have them.
- [ ] Then [Publishing](publishing.md).

# package.json

What Breezell reads from a plugin's `package.json`. The rest is an ordinary VS Code extension manifest.

## The `breezell` object

```json
"breezell": {
	"apiVersion": 1,
	"permissions": ["chat.events", "models.request"],
	"optionalPermissions": ["agent.hooks"],
	"source": "open"
}
```

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `apiVersion` | The API generation the plugin is written for: `1` |
| `permissions` | Every permission it uses ([Permissions](permissions.md)). One Breezell does not know refuses the install |
| `optionalPermissions` | Permissions only some versions know: an older Breezell leaves them out and installs the plugin. Check before use |
| `source` | `open` or `closed`: what the package holds and what the market shows ([Publishing](publishing.md)) |

Without a `breezell` object the extension is no plugin: `vscode.breezell` calls fail with `BreezellNotAPlugin`.

## Other fields that matter

- `"extensionKind": ["ui", "workspace"]`: in a remote (WSL, SSH) window the plugin runs on the user's computer,
  next to Breezell, so `vscode.breezell` is there even when the remote server is an older build. Window plugins need it.
- `activationEvents`: a plugin that registers agent tools, a send handler or a tool call handler should start
  with Breezell: `["onStartupFinished"]`. One that only answers its commands can start on them.
- `repository` (https): required for open source in the market.
- `icon`, `displayName`, `description`, `categories`: shown in the market ([Translations](translations.md) for other languages).

## `contributes.breezell`

| Key | What it declares | Permission | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skills` | Folders of skills for the agent | none | [The agent](agent.md#packs-skills-rules-mcp-servers) |
| `rules` | Markdown added to the AI's instructions | none | [The agent](agent.md#packs-skills-rules-mcp-servers) |
| `mcpServers` | MCP servers for the agent | `agent.tools` | [The agent](agent.md#packs-skills-rules-mcp-servers) |
| `tools` | Agent tools the plugin's code runs | `agent.tools` | [The agent](agent.md#agent-tools) |
| `windows` | Windows of the plugin's own | none | [Windows](windows.md) |
| `launcher` | How the plugin opens from Box | none | [below](#opening-a-plugin) |
| `restart` | A restart after install, update or removal | none (`app.forceRestart` to force) | [Restarting Breezell](restart.md) |
| `ui` | Buttons, pages, patches, tokens, fonts, a stylesheet, variants, fences, modes, settings | `ui.contribute`, `ui.modify`, `chat.render` | [Breezell's screens](ui.md) |

An entry Breezell cannot use is left out and the rest stays; the reason is logged, and `validate` tells you first.

## Opening a plugin

Users should not need a command to open a plugin. Declare how it opens:

```json
"contributes": {
	"breezell": {
		"launcher": { "command": "focusPlayer.open", "sidebar": true }
	},
	"commands": [{ "command": "focusPlayer.open", "title": "Open", "category": "Focus Player" }]
}
```

- `command`: one of the plugin's own `contributes.commands` (Breezell refuses any other),
  `window`: one of its windows (`"launcher": { "window": "timer" }`), or
  `signIn`: the page of one of its [sign-in tiles](ui.md#sign-in-tiles-new) in Box
  (`"launcher": { "signIn": "myService" }`, Breezell newer than 1.4.64).
- The plugin then gets an **Open** button in Breezell Console › Plugins (market card and Installed page).
- `sidebar` (default `true`): it is also listed by name under **Plugins** in the Box sidebar. Clicking it
  leaves Box for the editor and opens the plugin there (or opens its window; a `signIn` launcher opens its
  page in Box). Set `false` to stay out of the list.
- Plugins without an interface (packs, right-click commands) need no launcher.

# Models and providers

The user's chat models, from a plugin's own code: a request like one from the chat, the model picker,
and the user's custom APIs.

## A request (`models.request`)

```ts
const answer = await vscode.breezell.models.request({
	system: 'You review code briefly.',
	messages: [{ role: 'user', content: `Review this:\n${selection}` }],
	onText: soFar => panel.update(soFar),                    // streams
}, token);
console.log(answer.model, answer.text, answer.usage?.outputTokens);
```

### More than text

```ts
const checked = await vscode.breezell.models.request({
	model: { provider: 'openAICompatible', model: 'vision-model' },    // one of models.list()
	messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'What does this screen show?', images: [{ mimeType: 'image/png', data: base64 }] }],
	responseFormat: 'json',                                          // the answer parsed into .json
	maxOutputTokens: 400,
});
const result = checked.json as { broken: boolean; why: string };
```

- `model`: one of the model picker's models (`models.list()`) instead of the chat model. It needs no `models.select`.
- `images` on user messages: base64 without the `data:` prefix, png, jpeg, gif or webp, up to 8 per request.
  A model known not to read images refuses them (`BreezellInvalidRequest`).
- `responseFormat: 'json'`: the model is told to answer with one JSON value, and `json` holds it parsed
  (also out of a code fence). An answer with no JSON fails with `BreezellModelError`.
- `maxOutputTokens` (16 to 65,536) caps the answer; a model's reasoning counts too. Some relays
  (OpenAI Responses) do not apply it.

Rules of `models.request`:

- The first time a plugin uses it, Breezell asks the user. The user can revoke it at any time under
  **Plugins › Installed**.
- A request counts exactly like one the user sends in the chat: Breezell models are billed to the
  user's account, and a custom provider (Custom API) needs a plan that includes Custom API, as the
  server-signed entitlement says.
- The user's rules, skills and memories are not added, and no memory recall runs (no Super Memory quota is used).
- Each plugin may have at most 2 requests running and 20 a minute; a request holds at most 100
  messages and 200,000 characters.
- `onText` gets the whole text so far while the reply streams, `onReasoning` the model's reasoning so
  far while it thinks (models that reason and relays that pass it on), so a plugin can show it is
  working before any text. While a reply is silent Breezell checks that the API still answers (as it
  does for its own background requests): the request fails with `BreezellModelError` when the API
  stopped answering, and after five minutes in all.
- Errors carry a `name`: `BreezellNotSignedIn`, `BreezellPermissionDenied`, `BreezellRateLimited`,
  `BreezellNoModel`, `BreezellInvalidRequest`, `BreezellModelError`, `BreezellCancelled`,
  `BreezellBlocked` (the plugin is on the [blocklist](publishing.md#blocklist)).

## The model picker (`models.select`)

```ts
const models = await vscode.breezell.models.list();   // { provider, model, name, current }[]
await vscode.breezell.models.select({ provider: models[0].provider, model: models[0].model });
```

`select` switches the chat model exactly as the user's picker does, and only to a model it offers.

## Custom APIs

| Call | Permission | Gives |
|---|---|---|
| `providers.list()` | `providers.list` (normal) | Each custom API without keys: id, name, protocol, host, header names, pool size, models |
| `providers.listCustom()` | `providers.read` (dangerous) | Everything the settings page shows, **API keys** included. Only for an account whose plan includes Custom API (`BreezellPlanRequired` otherwise, without asking) |

Requests a plugin sends with those keys go to the provider directly and are billed to the user by it.

# An agent of your own

A plugin can answer conversations itself, with an agent it runs: a command-line agent the user installed
and signed in to, or a service of the plugin's own. Its models go in Breezell's model picker under one of
its [sign-in tiles](ui.md#sign-in-tiles-new), and a conversation on one of them is answered by the plugin,
not by a model Breezell sends requests to. The example is [Agent Bridge](https://github.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode/blob/main/plugins/examples/agent-bridge), which
connects the Claude Code the user installed and signed in to.

All of this needs a Breezell newer than 1.4.64.

## What the user sees

- A tile on **Box › Models › Sign in** that declares `"agent": true`. While the plugin lists models for it,
  they are in the chat's model picker under the tile, and the model menu offers their effort levels.
- In a conversation on one of them, the turn looks like one of Breezell's own models: the reply as it is
  written, its thinking, its tool calls as Breezell's own steps, approval cards, Stop, an error card with
  Retry, how long it worked.
- Breezell sends no model request for these turns and bills nothing for them. Answering with a plugin's
  agent is open to every signed-in user, as the user's own API keys (BYOK) are.

## Declaring it

```json
"breezell": { "apiVersion": 1, "permissions": ["ui.contribute", "chat.agent"] },
"contributes": {
	"configuration": {
		"properties": {
			"myAgent.enabled": { "type": "boolean", "default": false, "scope": "application", "description": "Connect My Agent" }
		}
	},
	"commands": [{ "command": "myAgent.check", "title": "Check My Agent Again" }],
	"breezell": {
		"ui": {
			"signIns": [{
				"id": "myAgent", "title": "My Agent", "icon": "sparkle",
				"setting": "myAgent.enabled", "command": "myAgent.check", "agent": true,
				"consent": { "title": "Connect My Agent?", "message": "What it reads, where what you send goes, and whose terms you follow." }
			}]
		}
	}
}
```

- `chat.agent` is dangerous: Breezell asks the first time the plugin registers its agent. Refused, its
  models are never offered, and `register` logs why.
- An older Breezell refuses to install a plugin with `chat.agent` in `permissions`. A plugin that is
  nothing without its agent can keep it there; one that does more puts it in `optionalPermissions`.

## Registering it and its models

```ts
const breezell = vscode.breezell;
context.subscriptions.push(breezell.agents.register('myAgent', { runTurn, stopSubagent }));
// Once connected; an empty list takes them out of the picker again.
await breezell.agents.setModels('myAgent', [
	{ id: 'fast', title: 'Fast', description: 'Quick answers', efforts: ['low', 'medium', 'high'] },
	{ id: 'deep', title: 'Deep' },
]);
```

- `setModels` replaces the list. List models only while the tile's switch is on and the agent can answer.
- `id`: letters, digits and `._:@+-[]`; `title` and `description` are shown in the picker.
- `family: 'claude'`: a model of a maker Breezell knows shows Breezell's own icon of that maker. Plugins
  never send logos.
- `efforts`: the levels the model takes. The model menu offers them; `turn.effort` is the one the user
  picked, and absent when they picked none (use the agent's own default then).
- `compacts: true`: the agent compresses its context when asked. Manual compress (the context ring)
  then asks it with a turn that has `compact`, instead of doing nothing. Breezell newer than 1.4.65.

## A turn

```ts
async function runTurn(turn: vscode.breezell.AgentTurn, reply: vscode.breezell.AgentReply, token: vscode.CancellationToken) {
	const run = myAgent.start({ resume: turn.session, folder: turn.folders[0], model: turn.model, prompt: promptOf(turn) });
	token.onCancellationRequested(() => run.stop());
	for await (const event of run.events()) {
		if (event.type === 'session') { reply.session(event.id); }
		if (event.type === 'text') { reply.text(event.text); }
		if (event.type === 'tool') { reply.tool({ id: event.id, name: event.name, status: event.status, view: viewOf(event) }); }
	}
	return { session: run.sessionId, entry: run.lastRecordId };
}
```

What a turn brings:

| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `conversationId` | The conversation, for `stopSubagent` and your own bookkeeping |
| `model` | The id of the model picked, one of those listed |
| `text` | What the user wrote (empty in a turn Breezell starts for `notices` alone) |
| `attachments` | What the user attached. Files and folders: their `path`, for the agent to open. Pictures and PDFs, pasted ones too: their bytes in `data` (base64 and its type), to give the agent as an image or a document. A code selection (`path`, `lines`), problems, console or terminal output, a quoted message, a skill and the like: `text`, what Breezell's own model is given of it. Anything else (a video): its name only |
| `folders` | The conversation's folders as URIs, the one it works in first |
| `session` | What the plugin said of its session in this conversation's last turn: go on in it |
| `effort` | The effort level picked, if any |
| `history` | What the conversation said that the agent has not seen, oldest first: another model's turns, or everything when there is no `session` to go on with (a new conversation for the agent, or one rewound or edited since). Tool calls are notes such as `[Breezell used read_file: a.ts (done)]` |
| `memories` | What Breezell remembers that bears on this message, as its own model gets it: put it in the agent's prompt |
| `continuing` | `{ after }`: the turn goes on in `session` after the agent's model request failed (see below). `text` is the message it was answering; there are no attachments |
| `notices` | Breezell's notices for the agent: how commands it ran in Breezell's terminal ended in the background |
| `mode` | The chat mode the user picked: `agent` (or absent) changes files and runs commands; `plan` reads and plans, and its plan goes to `callBreezellTool('update_plan', …)` (below), whose card's Execute starts an `agent` turn asking for it to be carried out; `analyze` reads and answers; `chat` answers. Breezell's tools for changes and commands are listed and run in `agent` only: turn the agent's own off in the other modes. Breezell newer than 1.4.65 |
| `compact` | The user chose Manual compress on the context ring (models listed with `compacts` only): compress the agent's context in `session` now, as it compresses its own, and nothing else. `text` is empty. Say how it went with `compaction`, and its size after with `usage` (`context`). Breezell newer than 1.4.65 |
| `rules` | The user's rules for this project, as Breezell's own model gets them (the project's rules file, else the global ones, and the plugins' rules for this model). Without `session`: give them to the new session once, where it keeps its standing instructions (they are not sent again with each message). With `session`: they changed since the session got them (`''`: removed); tell the agent once. Absent when there is nothing new. Breezell newer than 1.4.65 |
| `autoApprove` | `{ mcp }`: whether the user auto-approves MCP tools. Breezell never sees the calls an agent makes to MCP servers of its own before they run: an agent that cannot ask the user runs them only while `mcp` is true. Absent (an older Breezell): it does not. Breezell newer than 1.4.68 |

What the plugin writes:

| Member | What it does |
|---|---|
| `text(text, parent?)` | More of the reply. `parent`: the subagent call whose words they are |
| `reasoning(text, parent?)` | More of its reasoning, shown under Thinking |
| `thinking(tokens)` | A thought whose text the agent keeps hidden: Breezell shows Thinking with how long and about how many tokens. Not for a thought you give with `reasoning`, except one begun with `thinkingStarted`, whose size may come before its text |
| `thinkingStarted()` | Its model began a request whose thought the agent tells only after: Breezell shows Thinking from now until its words or a call come. The thought stays, with its time, when its text (`reasoning`) or its size (`thinking`) comes before the next call or the turn's end; otherwise there was none. Breezell newer than 1.4.68 |
| `tool(event)` | One of the agent's tool calls (below) |
| `session(id)` | The agent's own session: the next turn gets it as `turn.session`. Say it as soon as you know it |
| `usage({ context, models })` | What the agent's model requests used, once or more a turn. `context`: `tokens`, how much of its model's context its conversation now takes (its last request's input, cached parts too), and that model's `window`, for the chat's context ring. `models`: per model, the `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens` and `cacheWriteTokens` used since it last said this, for Box › Token usage and the reply's token count. Breezell newer than 1.4.65 |
| `compaction({ phase, trigger, preTokens, postTokens })` | The agent compresses its context: `started`, then `done` (its size before and after, as the agent says them) or `failed`. `trigger`: `manual` for a `compact` turn, `auto` when the agent compresses by itself. Breezell shows that it compresses ("Compressing…" on the ring for a `compact` turn, "Condensing" in the chat for the agent's own); the ring takes its size from `usage`, not from these. Breezell newer than 1.4.65 |
| `retrying({ attempt, maxAttempts, delayMs, error })` | The agent sends a failed model request again by itself: Breezell shows its reconnecting countdown until the agent's next event |
| `approve(request)` | Ask before a call runs (below) |
| `breezellTools()`, `callBreezellTool(name, input, toolUseId)` | Breezell's own tools for the agent (below) |

`runTurn` resolves with `{ session, entry, error, apiError }` or nothing. `session` is kept whatever
happens. `entry` is the id of the last record of the agent's own this turn made, so that importing the
session later adds only what came after it.

## Tool calls

Tell each call `running` as soon as it starts (and again to say how it goes), then `done` or `error`,
under the same `id`. With a `view`, Breezell draws it as its own tool of that kind; without one, it is a
row under its own name.

| `view.kind` | Drawn as |
|---|---|
| `read` | A file read: `path`, `uri`, `startLine`, `endLine`, `totalLines` |
| `edit` | An edit card with its diff: `path`, `uri`, `edits` (`oldString`, `newString`, `replaceAll`) |
| `create` | A new file: `path`, `uri`, `content` |
| `command` | A command card: `command`, `description`, `background`, `output` |
| `search`, `files`, `list` | A text search, the files a pattern found, a folder listed |
| `fetch`, `webSearch` | A page fetched, a web search |
| `todos` | The agent's to-do list |
| `subagent` | A subagent: `description`, `prompt`, `step`, `report`, `background`, `stopped`, `model` |
| `memories` | A lookup in Breezell's memories (`callBreezellTool('memories_recall')`) |
| `mcp` | A tool of one of the user's MCP servers in Breezell: `server`, `tool`. Drawn as Breezell's MCP row of that server, its approval card too |

- A file is drawn as Breezell's own only with its `uri`, as Breezell opens it: a `file:` or
  `vscode-remote:` URI of the window. `path` is the agent's own name of it.
- The agent's own file changes are its own: Breezell shows them, and never keeps, undoes or reviews them.
  To have changes reviewed as Breezell's own, let the agent make them with Breezell's edit tools (below).
- Tell a call while the agent is still writing it (its input so far), and its card grows with it.
- **Subagents.** A call with `view.kind: 'subagent'` gets a page of its own, as Breezell's subagents do.
  Its own words and calls carry `parent`: that call's id. `stopSubagent(conversationId, toolId)` is what
  Stop on its page runs; answer false if the agent cannot stop one subagent alone.

## Asking first

`reply.approve({ toolId, name, kind, title, input, reason, view })` shows Breezell's approval card on the
call's row (tell the call `running` first), unless the user's settings answer:

| `kind` | Decided by |
|---|---|
| `edit` | Auto-approve edits |
| `command` | Auto-approve terminal; with it off, the project's Always allow list (a dangerous command on it is asked all the same) |
| `other` | Auto-approve MCP tools |

It resolves false when the user refuses or the turn stops. Tell the agent the call was refused.

## Breezell's tools for the agent

`reply.breezellTools()` lists the tools this Breezell offers the agent: each `name`, its parameters as a
JSON schema, and for `run_terminal_cmd` the `shell` its commands run in (such as `windows | PowerShell`).
Offer them to the agent with descriptions of your own (an MCP server inside the plugin is one way), and
run its calls with `reply.callBreezellTool(name, input, toolUseId)`. Pass the agent's own id of the call
(the `id` of its tool event): Breezell then draws that row as its own tool's.

| Tool | What it does for the agent |
|---|---|
| `memories_recall` | Looks up what Breezell remembers, as Breezell's own model does |
| `run_terminal_cmd` | Runs a command in Breezell's terminal: the card has Open, Stop, live output and Move to background; a command still running after its wait goes on in the background |
| `await` | Waits on such a background command, or stops it |
| MCP tools | The tools of the user's MCP servers in Breezell, as Breezell's own model may use them in this mode: each listed with `mcpServer`, `mcpTool` and `description` beside its `name` and schema. Offer them under names of your own; call them by this `name`, and Breezell runs them with its own connection to the server (also from WSL, also signed-in servers). Ask first with `kind: 'other'` (Auto-approve MCP tools decides) and tell their calls with `view: { kind: 'mcp', server, tool }`. Breezell newer than 1.4.65 |
| `ask_question` | Asks the user the agent's questions with Breezell's question card, on the row of the agent's call (pass its `toolUseId`), in every mode. `questions`: each with an `id`, the `question`, at least two `options` (`id`, `label`) and `allow_multiple`. It waits for the user, whatever their auto-approve settings, and resolves with `answers` (per question, the labels picked or the user's own words); empty when they chose Skip. Breezell newer than 1.4.65 |
| `update_plan` | In `plan` mode: shows the agent's plan as Breezell's plan card, on the row of the agent's call (pass its `toolUseId`). Give `title`, `markdown` (the plan) and `plan`, its steps (`[{ step }]`, at least one), the card's to-dos. The user can edit it and chooses Execute. Not for the agent to call itself |
| `edit_file`, `write_to_file` | Changes a file or creates one through Breezell's editor: a snapshot before it, the change in the editor to keep or undo, a step of Code Review, Auto-accept, Open file when editing, and the lint and type errors it leaves in the result |

- When you offer the terminal or the edit tools, turn the agent's own shell or edit tools off, so that
  every command and change goes through Breezell.
- A failure comes back as a result with `isError`, never as a thrown error. Give its `text` to the agent.
- Commands that end in the background come back as `turn.notices` with the next message. When one ends
  while the conversation is idle, Breezell starts a turn of its own: `text` is empty and `notices` says
  what ended.

## Failures, retries and Stop

- Stop cancels `token`: stop the agent and return.
- A thrown error, or `error` in the result, is shown as the error card after what was written.
- `apiError`: the error came from the agent's model request, of this kind (`rate_limit`, `overloaded`,
  `server_error`, `unknown` for a dropped connection, `stalled`, or one a new attempt cannot get past,
  such as `billing_error`). Breezell then waits as it does for its own requests and calls `runTurn` again
  in `session` with `continuing`, as often as its own retry settings say. Ask the agent to continue from
  where it stopped, not to start over. Retry on the error card does the same.
- When the agent retries by itself, say so with `retrying`, and Breezell shows the same countdown.

## The agent's own conversations

`agents.importConversation(tileId, { session, folder, title, model, messages })` brings one of the agent's
own conversations (one session) into the window that has its folder open, as a conversation that goes on
in that session. Messages are user, assistant and tool messages, oldest first, each with the `entry` of
the agent's record it comes from (a tool message can carry a `view` and a subagent's messages). The same
session again adds only what came after the last record the conversation shows.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `created` | A new conversation |
| `updated` | It got the session's newer messages |
| `unchanged` | Nothing new, or no record to go on from |
| `deleted` | The user deleted it: it stays deleted |
| `busy` | It runs a turn now: try later |
| `elsewhere` | This window does not have its folder open |

`agents.onDidDeleteConversations` tells which of the plugin's conversations the user deleted, with their
sessions and folders. Delete the agent's own copies only when the user asked for that (Agent Bridge has
an option for it, off by default, that asks before it turns on).

## Rules

- Never read, keep or pass on the user's credentials for the agent. Let the user sign in to it
  themselves, in its own app, and run it as it was published.
- Follow the terms of whoever makes the agent, also for its name and logos: a tile takes a codicon,
  never an image.
- Do not name the tile, its settings or its buttons after Breezell.
- Say in the consent what the plugin reads, where what the user sends goes, and that Breezell's
  approval cards decide the agent's actions.

Limits: [Limits](limits.md#calls).

# Permissions

Every permission: whether it is on from the start or asked for, and what it gives.

A plugin declares every permission it uses in `package.json` (`"breezell": { "permissions": [...] }`),
as an Android app does in its manifest. Nothing undeclared is ever usable, and the market lists what
each plugin declares before it is installed.

| Permission | Kind | Granted |
|---|---|---|
| `chat.events` | normal | On from the start; the user can turn it off |
| `models.request` | dangerous | Asked for the first time the plugin uses it |
| `models.select` | normal | On from the start; the user can turn it off |
| `chat.read` | dangerous | Asked for the first time the plugin uses it |
| `chat.send` | dangerous | Asked for the first time the plugin uses it |
| `chat.approve` | dangerous | Asked for the first time the plugin uses it |
| `providers.read` | dangerous | Asked for the first time the plugin uses it, and only for an account whose plan includes Custom API |
| `providers.list` | normal | On from the start; the user can turn it off. Never a key |
| `agent.tools` | dangerous | "Agent tool registration": asked when the plugin first registers a tool, or when a plugin with MCP servers first runs |
| `agent.hooks` | dangerous | Asked when the plugin first registers a tool call handler or listens to tool runs: it sees what the agent passes (file paths, edits, commands) and the results |
| `app.restart` | normal | On from the start; the user can turn it off. The user still answers each request |
| `app.forceRestart` | dangerous | Asked the first time the plugin forces a restart; if refused, the plugin asks each time instead |
| `editor.read` | dangerous | The plugin asks with `requestPermission`. A plugin is an extension, so VS Code's API reaches open files whatever this says: this is how it says that it does, and how the user tells it not to |
| `chat.input` | dangerous | Asked for the first time the plugin reads the chat box |
| `chat.intercept` | dangerous | Asked when the plugin registers a send handler |
| `chat.agent` | dangerous | Asked the first time the plugin registers an agent: in conversations where the user picked one of its models, what they send goes to the plugin, which writes the replies (Breezell newer than 1.4.64) |
| `ui.contribute` | normal | On from the start; the user can turn it off, which takes the plugin's buttons, pages and modes out of Breezell's screens |
| `ui.modify` | dangerous | Asked when a plugin that declares `ui.patches`, `ui.tokens`, `ui.variants`, `ui.fonts`, `ui.stylesheet`, a companion or a page in the title bar first runs |
| `chat.render` | dangerous | Asked when a plugin that declares `ui.renderers` first runs: a drawn code fence hands the plugin its text |
| `ui.overlay` | dangerous | Asked the first time the plugin opens a window of `"kind": "overlay"`: a small window that floats above every app. Ask while the user is in Breezell (`requestPermission`), or the question waits in a window they left |
| `activity.read` | normal | On from the start; the user can turn it off. What the agent is doing (its step, the file name, the model, how long) and the build or test task: never what messages say |

- A permission only some versions of Breezell know goes in `"breezell": { "optionalPermissions": [...] }`:
  an older Breezell leaves it out and installs the plugin all the same, where a permission it does not
  know in `permissions` would refuse it. Check before using what it gives.
- A dangerous permission is asked for once, when the plugin first uses it; the answer is kept. While
  the user has not allowed it, its calls fail with `BreezellPermissionDenied` and the plugin should
  say what it cannot do.
- On the plugin's page (**Plugins › Installed**) the user switches each permission on and off, or
  all of them at once. Turning one off stops it at once, including events the plugin listens to.
- Ask only for what the plugin needs: review looks harder at plugins that read or send messages or
  approve tool calls, and at closed source ones above all.
- `chat.read` gives what the user sees in the chat: never Breezell's prompts, text only the model
  sees, hidden messages or other workspaces' conversations. A tool's parameters and result are cut
  at 20,000 characters. `chat.send` sends at most 10 messages a minute and refuses a busy
  conversation; its messages are billed like the user's own.
- `chat.read` also says how many commands a conversation runs in the background, and the tokens its
  replies used as the provider reported them: nothing about money, plans or quota.
- `chat.agent` gives the plugin the conversations where the user picked one of its models: each message
  sent with that model, what Breezell recalls for it, and what was said there before that the agent has
  not seen. Never other conversations. The agent's tool calls go through Breezell's approval cards when
  it asks, and answering with a plugin's agent is open to every signed-in user, like their own API keys. See
  [An agent of your own](own-agent.md).
- `providers.read` hands out the custom APIs' keys: a plugin can call those APIs itself, outside
  Breezell, and the providers bill the user. It works only for an account whose Breezell plan
  includes Custom API; otherwise the call fails with `BreezellPlanRequired` and the user is not
  asked. It never gives Breezell's own account or other providers' keys.

## Checking and asking

```ts
const breezell = vscode.breezell;
if (!breezell?.permissions.includes('agent.hooks')) {
	return; // an older Breezell left the optional permission out
}
if (await breezell.permissionState('editor.read') === 'ask') {
	await breezell.requestPermission('editor.read');   // asks now, at a moment of your choosing
}
breezell.onDidChangePermissions(() => refresh());       // the user switched one on the plugin's page
```

- `permissionState(p)` is `granted`, `denied` or `ask` and asks no one.
- `requestPermission(p)` asks when it is the first time and returns whether it is allowed.
- A dangerous permission's first call asks by itself; a refused one fails with `BreezellPermissionDenied`.
- The user can turn any permission off at any time, also a normal one: handle the error where you call.

# Phone plugins

A phone plugin changes the **Breezell phone app**: a theme of its own, or a file of a kind shown another way than as
